commits.subject: fix(android): localize the update-time label and reach the provider fallback
fix(android): show the quality band and score again and warn about conflicting sources
fix(android): render the home-screen widget in the app language
fix(wear): send the watch status, category and notice in the phone language

items.what_changed: HEAD still had every residual: RouteSnapshotCache.lastProvider() returned the literal "Nessun provider" (so the localized provider_unavailable fallback in MainActivity was unreachable), accessibleUpdateTime() in app/src/main/java/it/binario/app/data/TrainDataSource.kt built "aggiornato alle HH:mm"/"mai aggiornato", RouteWidgetProvider.kt carried ~30 Italian literals (meta labels, status column, TalkBack, direction/target via Direction.label/WidgetTargetType.label, persisted failure text) and AndroidWearSnapshotContract.kt sent Italian enum labels plus "Programmato", "dati non disponibili in tempo reale", "Non disponibile". Fixes: lastProvider() now returns String? (null when nothing cached) and TrainViewModel.currentProviderLabel() falls through to the UI fallback; the update time is a UiMessage (UPDATE_TIME_AT/UPDATE_TIME_NEVER, new keys update_time_at/update_time_never in all 5 catalogues) rendered with .localized() in Compose and .resolve(resources) in the widget; new EnumLabelResources.kt holds the shared enum→R.string table (MainActivity's localizedLabel() helpers now delegate to it); new widget/WidgetStrings.kt (TrainShareStrings pattern) is resolved once per render and drives compactMeta, accessibleDataSummary, statusLabel/displayStatus, row TalkBack, direction and target labels (37 new widget_*/snapshot_warning_* keys in 5 languages); widget state persists the TrainCategory enum name (legacy Italian label mapped back) and the failure as UiMessage key + ISO arguments (legacy free text dropped for the generic label); the Wear encoder takes a WearSnapshotStrings catalogue resolved from resources by WearSnapshotPublisher (confidence, category, status, scheduled badge, data_status_unavailable notice, new wear_payload_value_unavailable). Voice feedback (E2E-12/AND-NEW-6) was already localized at HEAD (PlannerVoiceFeedbackResources.kt) — no change. Removed now-unused Direction.label and WidgetTargetType.label.
items.tests: UpdateTimeMessageTest (key + Europe/Rome time; never-updated), WidgetStateMetadataTest rewritten (Italian and English catalogues: compact meta, TalkBack data summary, row TalkBack), WidgetChangeHighlightTest adjusted to the new displayStatus(service, confidence, strings) signature with an English expectation (SCHED.), new WidgetFailureCodecTest (round trip with LocalDate/LocalTime args; legacy Italian text → null), AndroidWearSnapshotContractTest: golden test now builds the catalogue from the real values/strings.xml and still matches the v1 fixture, new test builds it from values-en and asserts Delayed/On time/Scheduled/Operator primary source/Live data unavailable/Not available. Without the fix every new test fails (the new APIs do not exist; the old code produced the Italian texts the English assertions reject). The existing widget tests that pinned Italian literals had their expectations changed in the same commit (9fb6542). The widget/Wear resource-resolution glue (WidgetStrings.from(context), WearSnapshotStrings.from(resources), RemoteViews rendering) is static only.

items.what_changed: HEAD still had the regression: TrainViewModel.currentQualityBand()/currentQualityScore() were dead and the status line/detail screen showed only the confidence. MainActivity now renders "<band> · <score>/100 · <confidence>" through a TrainViewModel.localizedQualityLabel() composable with new quality_band_* keys (6) and quality_band_score in 5 languages, used by both DataStatusLine and the detail/share header (the old currentConfidenceLabel() format). AND-NEW-5's conflict warning: RouteSnapshot.advisoryMessage() now returns the new ROUTE_SOURCE_CONFLICT UiMessage (key route_source_conflict, 5 languages) when SnapshotWarning.SOURCE_CONFLICT is among the quality warnings, with the coverage-fallback caveat keeping priority; the fallback caveat and the GTFS-expiry message were already shown at HEAD via advisoryMessage()/RouteFailureReason.uiMessage() (upstream e70941e). Dead helpers removed: RouteSnapshotCache.lastConfidence() and the last_confidence write (Italian label persisted for nothing), TrainService.accessibleSummary, CommuterAlert.accessibleSummary, MobilityPreferences.accessibleSummary, StationMonitor.accessibleSummary and the Italian enum labels that only fed them (AlertRepeat.label, StationMonitorMode.label); unused Instant/DateTimeFormatter imports in TrainDataSource.kt. Docs: README (snapshots expose the quality score; widget exposes quality score) and CHANGELOG (widget/Wear texts resolved at the UI boundary, no Italian copy in persisted state) are true again after these commits, so no doc text needed changing; a scan of values-en for Italian leftovers found none and the finding named no specific mistranslation.
items.tests: RouteFailureMessageTest gained a test for advisoryMessage(): null without warnings, ROUTE_SOURCE_CONFLICT with a conflict, ROUTE_COVERAGE_FALLBACK winning when both apply (fails without the fix: the key does not exist and the old function returned null for conflicts). AndroidStringResourceParityTest allowlist extended with quality_band_score (format-only). The Compose status-line rendering itself is static only (no Compose runtime in the harness).

findings.description: The finding names the Wear payload's status/notice. The branch localizes the status, the category, the source label and the notice of the *unavailable* payload, but `operational()` still sends `put("notice", optional(snapshot.notice.orEmpty(), 180))`, i.e. the data layer's Italian prose (e.g. RfiLiveRouteDataSource: "Ritardi dai tabelloni RFI. Sono mostrate le fermate di partenza e arrivo richieste.", ViaggiaTrenoStationAdapter: "Dati live ViaggiaTreno: partenze da … verso …", DataReconciliation: "Fonti concordanti non disponibili per N campo/i …"). The watch shows that text verbatim (wear/src/main/java/it/binario/wear/WearMainActivity.kt:83 and tile/BinarioTileService.kt:89), so the normal (non-error) path of the watch still shows Italian in en/de/fr/es. The phone UI no longer renders snapshot.notice at all (MainActivity has no reader), so the Wear payload is the only surface that still leaks it. The colleague's report does not mention this path.
findings.suggested_fix: Send a catalogue-resolved text instead of the raw snapshot.notice: extend WearSnapshotStrings with the localized advisories (route_coverage_fallback, route_source_conflict via UiMessageKey, or the SnapshotWarning labels via the shared labelRes()) and in operational() put `notice` = `snapshot.advisoryMessage()?.let { strings.advisoryNotices.getValue(it.key) } ?: snapshot.qualityWarnings.firstOrNull()?.let { strings.warningLabels.getValue(it) }.orEmpty()` (the contract README allows an empty notice). Update the golden expectation in AndroidWearSnapshotContractTest / contracts/wear-snapshot/v1/android-to-wear-v1.json (the golden snapshot has no warnings, so the notice becomes ""), keep the truncation test by driving it through a long localized advisory or by asserting the 180-char trim on the new field source, and add an English-catalogue assertion for the notice. Alternatively drop the data-layer notice from the payload entirely with the same test updates; either way no Italian data-layer prose must reach the payload.

findings.description: WidgetService.accessibleLabel() picks the delay wording with `delayMinutes > 0` regardless of status. ViaggiaTrenoRealtimeAdapter keeps delayMinutes for verified cancelled trains (status = CANCELLED, delayMinutes = delay), so TalkBack would read "Soppresso +12 min" / "Cancelled +12 min" for a cancelled train.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `status == ServiceStatus.DELAYED && delayMinutes > 0` for the delayed branch so a cancelled service is announced only as cancelled.

findings.description: The widget tests feed hand-written catalogues, so the actual widget_* resource values (e.g. a typo in widget_confidence_infrastructure_primary) are only compile-checked through R and key-checked by the parity test, never content-checked; the Wear test in the same branch already shows how to build the catalogue from the real values/strings.xml.
findings.suggested_fix: Advisory: add one test that builds WidgetStrings from app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml (and values-en) with the same DOM reader used by AndroidWearSnapshotContractTest and asserts the original Italian meta line, so the resources themselves are covered.

The 7-day gap / 7-day span rule is a judgement call: a pack whose last real period is shorter than a week would be understated by a few days; a works closure longer than a week followed by a real period is handled. 3) TW-11 widens Android's next-day window to 24 h as iOS; the widget/Wear snapshots already handled next-day departures from the previous 6 h window, so no consumer change was needed. 4) TW-18: the normaliser keeps server-acceptable forms as the server would store them ('S9-25015'), and reduces only otherwise-rejected labelled forms to their trailing train number; the Alexa sync itself is still not wired. 5) The existing comment references to 'Opus audit N-M12' in EmbeddedGtfsRouteAdapter/ItalianRailServiceCalendar predate this work and were kept as the repository's own audit-ID convention.

findings.description: The catalogue now yields null instead of the text "null", but WidgetConfiguration (lines 121-122) and CustomStationStore (lines 58-59) persist a copy of the station and decode the code with `.ifBlank { null }` only, so a widget or custom station saved on a device before this fix keeps railwayCode/trenitaliaLocationId = "null" until it is reconfigured. The plan listed both files under FS-1. Practical impact is small (such stations have no real code, so live lookups fail either way), hence minor.
findings.suggested_fix: In both decoders treat the literal "null" like blank, e.g. `parts[4].takeUnless { it.isBlank() || it == "null" }`, so upgraded installs self-heal on the next read; add a one-line decode test for a legacy "null" entry.

findings.description: With the 24 h window a Thursday 14:00 search correctly lists Friday 08:05, but the phone row (lines 1993/2657), the widget (expectedDeparture only) and the Wear payload (service{n}Scheduled HH:mm) carry no day hint, so the next morning's trains look like today's. iOS renders a bare HH:mm string too (SQLiteGTFSJourneyRepository.timeString), so this is a pre-existing cross-platform gap that the fix makes far more visible, not a regression; the StopAlarmPlanner and board reconciler use the full LocalDateTime and stay correct (a next-day 08:05 is 24 h away from today's board row, outside scheduleTolerance).
findings.suggested_fix: Advisory follow-up (all platforms): add a 'domani'/date marker when scheduledDepartureDateTime.toLocalDate() != query.serviceDate (phone list, widget row, Wear snapshot field). Not required for this package.

findings.description: Positive terms are OR-ed (`positives.any { it.kind.matches(date) }`), so a text such as "nei giorni lavorativi dal lunedì al venerdì" now runs on Saturday (LAVORATIV* = Mon–Sat matches) whereas at the base branch only the Mon–Fri range was recognised. The same already holds for "feriale dal lunedì al venerdì", no fixture or real text with 'lavorativ' exists in the repo, and 'lavorativo' = 'feriale' is what the plan asked for, so advisory only.
findings.suggested_fix: Optional: when a clause contains both a generic term (FERIALE/LAVORATIV*/FESTIV*) and an explicit day set, intersect rather than union them; add a test for "Lavorativi dal lunedì al venerdì" on a Saturday. Out of this item's scope.

findings.description: afternoonPhrases covers 'di sera', 'stasera', 'del pomeriggio' etc., but the very common 'domani sera alle 8' / 'domani pomeriggio alle 3' (bare 'sera'/'pomeriggio' after a date word) still yield 08:00 / 03:00; same for 'tomorrow evening at 8' and 'morgen abend um 8' ('abends'/'am abend' are listed, 'abend' alone is not).
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'domani sera', 'domani pomeriggio', 'dopodomani sera', 'tomorrow evening', 'tomorrow afternoon', 'morgen abend', 'demain soir', 'manana por la tarde' (or simply a trailing-word match for sera/pomeriggio/notte after a date word) to afternoonPhrases with test cases.

findings.description: The fallback chain matches the plan, but note the real data: ARST shows 'Linea SASSARI-ALGHERO' / 'Linea MONSERRATO-ISILI' as the train number (iOS does the same via route_short_name, so parity holds), and for SNCF Android now shows the numeric headsign ('105241') while iOS still shows route_short_name ('A01'): a cross-platform divergence where Android is the better one. A number search for '445'/'446' now returns every TFT run on that line (bounded by limits).
findings.suggested_fix: No change needed here; file a follow-up to add the numeric-headsign step to iOS's number derivation (SQLiteGTFSJourneyRepository rawNumber) so both platforms show the same SNCF number.

Acceptable (fail-closed is the right direction for a security fix); informational.

result.concerns: 1) Behaviour change visible to Italian watch users too: the informational data-source prose ("Ritardi dai tabelloni RFI...", "Dati live ViaggiaTreno: partenze da...") no longer appears on the watch in any language; the watch now shows only the phone's advisory (unofficial coverage source / conflicting sources) or the first snapshot quality warning, and nothing for a clean snapshot. The contract README documents this; the field semantics (bounded string, may be empty) are unchanged, so no schemaVersion bump. 2) The golden fixture contracts/wear-snapshot/v1/android-to-wear-v1.json changed (notice ""); the Wear decoder tests that consume it are green, and the companion/iOS fixtures are untouched. CI's android-ci path filter includes contracts/wear-snapshot/**, as expected. 3) The first warning is chosen with qualityWarnings.firstOrNull(), mirroring the widget's compactMeta; for a freshly evaluated snapshot the set is DataQuality's insertion-ordered linkedSetOf, so the choice is deterministic. 4) strings.advisoryNotices.getValue(key) would throw if a future advisoryMessage() key were not added to WearSnapshotStrings.advisoryKeys; WearSnapshotPublisher.publish() already wraps operational() in runCatching and falls back to the unavailable payload, so the failure mode is a watch showing 'unavailable', not a crash; the test builds its catalogue from the same advisoryKeys list. 5) Static only: the watch's rendering of an empty notice (WearMainActivity hides blank text; the tile prints an empty line) and the widget's RemoteViews TalkBack are verified by reading, since Compose/RemoteViews are compiled but never executed in this harness. 6) The resource-backed widget test keeps its own private strings.xml reader (the third such private copy in the test tree, next to the Wear contract test and the parity test); I chose that over extracting a shared helper to avoid touching unrelated tests.
